items.title: EU proposes ban on Russian-insured tankers in 22nd sanctions package
items.summary: European Commission President von der Leyen outlined on Nov 23 a package that would bar tankers insured in Russia, stop EU firms from servicing Russian energy infrastructure including refineries, and add more than 70 vessels to the shadow-fleet list. It needs unanimous approval from all 27 member states. S&P data showed no oil or chemical tankers discharging in the Netherlands in November carried Russian cover.

items.title: Week 47: Baltic clean index 2,581; one-year MR charter $34,000/day
items.summary: Compass Maritime's Nov 23 report puts the Baltic Clean Tanker Index at 2,581, against 2,592 a week earlier and 811 a year ago, while the dirty index rose to 5,081 from 4,483. Its one-year time-charter assessment for MRs eased to $34,000/day from $36,500, with LR1s unchanged at $53,500 and VLCCs down to $184,500 from $234,000.

items.title: Product tanker spot earnings down 4.8% on the week, led by Atlantic MRs
items.summary: Makai Research's week 47 report says product tanker spot earnings fell 4.8% week on week and are 13.4% below the late-October peak. MRs accounted for most of the decline, with Atlantic MR earnings falling sharply while Pacific MRs held near early-October levels; LRs slipped 2.1% and Handies were the only class to gain, on Med/Med business.

items.title: Hafnia drops pursuit of Torm; product tanker shares down 7.2% on week
items.summary: Nortilus reports that Hafnia has ended its pursuit of Torm. In week 47, listed product tanker equities fell 7.2% and crude tanker shares 4.3%, though both remain about 17% higher month to date; it also cites VLCC earnings down 18% to about $293,000/day.

items.title: Frontline Q3 profit $641.4m; Q4 LR2/Aframax booked at $190,800/day
items.summary: Frontline earned $641.4m ($2.88/share) in Q3 on revenue of $921.3m, including a $111.2m gain on two VLCC sales; adjusted profit was $530.9m versus $580.2m in Q2. For Q4 it has booked 68% of VLCC spot days at $562,600/day, 69% of Suezmax days at $324,300/day and 68% of LR2/Aframax days at $190,800/day, and says full-quarter rates will come in lower because of ballast days. Dividend is $2.38/share.

items.title: Jones Act waiver extended a third time, to cargoes loaded by Feb 14
items.summary: DHS has extended the Jones Act waiver for 90 days from Nov 16; covered products must be loaded by 11:59 pm ET on Feb 14, 2027. The list of 237 HTS codes is unchanged and includes crude, refined products, LPG/LNG, fertilizers, ethyl alcohol for fuel, sulfur-based chemicals, anhydrous ammonia and biodiesel; the vessel-availability and reporting steps also stay the same.

items.title: Hanwha Philly cuts steel on first of four Jones Act MR chemical tankers
items.summary: Construction began Nov 17 on the first of four 49,500 dwt Jones Act MR product/chemical tankers for Hanwha Shipping, built to IMO Type 2 and 3 standards, with an optional 18-segregation configuration. Deliveries are scheduled for 2029–2030; Hanwha says it is the first US-built MR in nearly a decade.

items.title: Hormuz: IRGC says two tankers struck mines on an 'unauthorized route'
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire while using a route not coordinated with Iran, and the army said it had deployed new systems to control the strait. The claim has not been independently confirmed. Iranian officials also said the country can withstand the US naval blockade.

items.title: Houthis claim drone attack on Saudi Ras Tanura refinery
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted four drones over the area but did not confirm a hit on the plant; separately, Saudi Civil Defense said a strike on a Riyadh tower injured 11 people.

items.title: Houthis threaten Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports over Hodeidah
items.summary: The Houthis said Wednesday they would target Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports if Saudi Arabia attacks Hodeidah, and urged shipping companies to withdraw vessels. The Saudi-led coalition said it struck targets at Hodeidah on Wednesday; on Tuesday a Houthi drone hit a Riyadh tower, injuring at least 11 people according to Saudi authorities.

items.title: Hormuz: UKMTO reports three vessels hit by projectiles; crews accounted for
items.summary: UKMTO said three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with all crew accounted for. The IRGC separately said it targeted a container ship near the strait; that claim was not independently confirmed in the report.

items.title: Libya: Ukrainian drone strike on Russian warship kills two officers; Italy objects
items.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship at an eastern Libyan port killed two Libyan naval officers, and the Libyan National Army has vowed retaliation. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani criticized Ukraine over the strikes on Russian ships in the Mediterranean.

items.title: Houston Ship Channel: deep-draft transits up 12% in October
items.summary: Port Houston's November report shows 1,628 deep-draft transits in October (up 12% year on year) and 19,251 barge transits (down 2%). September foreign tonnage was 22.3m short tons, up 13%, with exports up 16%; the region handled 32% of US crude exports through September. Port Houston's terminals moved a record 415,326 TEU in October, up 14%.

items.title: Bunkers: Houston VLSFO $850.50/t, Fujairah $993.50/t
items.summary: Compass's Nov 23 report puts VLSFO at $850.50/t in Houston, $794.50 in Rotterdam, $993.50 in Fujairah and $1,019.50 in Singapore; MGO is $1,407.50/t in Houston.

items.title: Tuesday Nov 24 close: Dow 50,018.70 (+0.85%), S&P 500 7,201.09 (−0.50%), Nasdaq 23,733.54 (−1.48%)
items.summary: In the latest completed session, the Dow rose 423.39 points while the S&P 500 fell 36.08 and the Nasdaq 356.02, with chip stocks weighing after Nvidia fell 5.9%. By 1:37 pm ET Wednesday, Yahoo Finance showed the Dow up 0.40% at 50,217.17 and the Nasdaq down 1.19% as the tech selloff continued. US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early Friday.

items.title: Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%; October core PCE inflation 3.3% year on year
items.summary: Third-quarter growth was revised to a 4.3% annual rate from 3.4%, against a 3.5% consensus. October PCE prices rose 0.3% on the month and 3.8% on the year; core PCE rose 0.3% and 3.3%, slightly above the 3.2% expected.

items.title: 10-year yield eases to 4.82%; futures price about 97–98% odds of a December Fed hike
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.82% mid-morning Wednesday, down 7 basis points from about 4.90%, and the 30-year was 5.24%. CME FedWatch showed roughly 97–98% odds of a 25 bp hike at the Dec 9–10 meeting and about 63% odds of another in January.

items.title: Oil: Brent settles $91.40 (+2.27%), WTI $82.05 (+2.35%)
items.summary: Brent rose $2.03 and January WTI $1.88 on Tuesday as attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and a Houthi strike on Riyadh added risk. Gains were limited by supply concerns: Deutsche Bank said October inventory builds imply a global surplus of about 1.7m b/d.

items.title: Dell and Workday beat estimates; Deere misses
items.summary: Dell reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $9.45 on $54.94B revenue, versus estimates of $6.59 and $49.32B, and announced a $25B buyback. Workday posted adjusted EPS of $2.82 against $2.74 expected, while Deere's Q4 adjusted EPS of $3.89 missed the $4.03 consensus.

items.title: US expected to announce new tariffs on China, EU and 14 other economies
items.summary: Sources told AP the US Trade Representative is expected to announce tariffs on 16 economies after a subsidies investigation, with timing still subject to change. A White House official cited 20% for China and 15% for the EU, effective January at the earliest, with exemptions for energy and some food, chips and pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Asia lower Wednesday: Nikkei −1,633 to 57,011; Hang Seng −253
items.summary: Asian markets fell with chip stocks, with the Nikkei down 1,633 points to 57,011, Shanghai down 71 to 3,476 and the Hang Seng down 253 to 21,966. In early European trade the DAX was 40 points lower at 24,977 and the FTSE 100 18 points higher at 10,485.

items.title: Ukraine: Russian strike in Odesa region kills two; Putin warns of retaliation over refinery attacks
items.summary: Odesa Governor Oleh Kiper said a Russian strike killed two people and injured three, including a child. Putin said Ukraine has continued striking Russian oil refineries despite US requests to stop and called retaliation inevitable.

items.title: Gaza: Israeli strike kills head of Hamas interior security service
items.summary: Israel killed Hamas colonel Mohammad Abuelouf, who led the group's interior security service, in a strike on Beach camp in Gaza City; Hamas-run health officials and medics said his wife and two children were also killed.

items.title: Huawei convicted of trade-secret conspiracy and bank fraud, acquitted of racketeering
items.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn found Huawei guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets and of bank fraud but not of racketeering. Huawei said it will pursue all available legal options.

items.title: Alaska Senate: Sullivan concedes to Peltola
items.summary: Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan conceded the Alaska Senate race to Democrat Mary Peltola, who leads by more than four points, after the Justice Department dropped its suit over certification.

items.title: FAA ground stop traced to misconfigured router
items.summary: Investigators linked last week's nationwide FAA ground stop to a new router whose settings flooded older equipment; a source said investigators are about 90% sure no bad actor was involved. FAA and Transportation Department leaders face congressional hearings next week.

items.title: Sudan: drone strikes on Damazin kill at least 19
items.summary: Drone strikes on Damazin in Blue Nile state killed at least 19 people and wounded 15; a Sudanese lawyers' group blamed the RSF. Sudan's government also rejected an Ethiopian mediation offer.

items.title: Solomon Islands and Australia sign treaty barring foreign military bases
items.summary: The two countries signed a security treaty that rules out a foreign military or security base in the Solomon Islands. A diplomat said the 2022 Solomon Islands–China security pact will not be renewed when it expires next year.

items.title: Broncos (8–2) at Steelers Friday, 2:00 pm CT on Prime Video
items.summary: Denver is 8–2, tied with Kansas City for first in the AFC West. The Broncos play at Pittsburgh (6–4) on Black Friday, Nov 27, at 3:00 pm ET / 2:00 pm CT, streamed on Prime Video.

items.title: Texans (4–6) host Ravens Sunday at noon CT on CBS
items.summary: Houston is 4–6 and second in the AFC South behind Jacksonville (7–3). The Texans host Baltimore (4–7) on Sunday, Nov 29, at 1:00 pm ET / 12:00 pm CT on CBS.

items.title: Davis Cup: Musetti beats Hong 6–0, 7–6(5) to put Italy 1–0 up on South Korea
items.summary: In the Bologna quarterfinal, Lorenzo Musetti won the opening singles in 1 hour 34 minutes, with Flavio Cobolli to face Soonwoo Kwon next. The winner meets the Czech Republic in Friday's semifinal.

items.title: Davis Cup: Czechia beats Canada 2–0 to reach Bologna semifinals
items.summary: Tomas Machac beat Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 and Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4), 6-2, so the doubles was not needed. Canada played without Denis Shapovalov and Gabriel Diallo, who withdrew injured.
